purpose: Carbinoxamine is used to relieve allergy symptoms like runny nose, sneezing, itchy or watery eyes, and skin itching. It can also help with symptoms of hay fever and other respiratory allergies. Sometimes it is used to relieve symptoms of the common cold.
how_it_works: Your body releases a chemical called histamine when it encounters something you are allergic to, and histamine is what causes those uncomfortable allergy symptoms. Carbinoxamine works by blocking histamine from attaching to receptors in your body, which helps reduce or stop those symptoms. Think of it like putting a lock on a door so histamine cannot get in and cause trouble.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is drowsiness or feeling sleepy, which is why some people take it at bedtime. You may also experience dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, blurred vision, constipation, or difficulty urinating. These effects are more common with this older type of antihistamine.
warnings: Because this medicine causes drowsiness, do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires you to be fully alert until you know how it affects you. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medication as it can make drowsiness much worse. Talk to your doctor before taking it if you have glaucoma, an enlarged prostate, breathing problems, or if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. It is not recommended for children under 2 years old.
typical_dosing: For adults, a typical dose is 4 to 8 mg taken by mouth three to four times a day. Extended-release forms are taken less frequently, usually every 12 hours. Always follow your doctor or pharmacist's exact instructions, as dosing can vary based on the specific product and your individual needs.
